title: Erdos problem #107: a counterexample to the Erdos-Szekeres conjecture
statement: Find points in the plane, no three on a line, with at least 2^(c-1) + 1 points but no c + 1 of them in convex position, for some c: a counterexample to the Erdos-Szekeres ('happy ending') conjecture that any 2^(n-2) + 1 points in general position contain a convex n-gon. The conjecture holds for n <= 6, so a counterexample has at least 33 points. A valid counterexample scores 1 (Erdos offered $500 for the problem).
submission: Text file: one point per line, two integer coordinates separated by a space or a comma.
